title: Finite finitely presented direct image reflects finite presentation
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $f_*\mathcal F$ for its Zariski direct image, defined on an open $V\subseteq Y$ by $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$, with $\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting through $f^\sharp(V):\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$. If $f_*\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, then $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation].

source.place: Tag 05B4, label lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, reverse implication and its affine proof.

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq Y$ be any affine open and put $U=f^{-1}V$, $R=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $S=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $M=\mathcal F(U)$. By the definition of a finite morphism, $U$ is affine and $S$ is finite as an $R$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the affine opens $U,V$: its containment hypothesis is $f(U)\subseteq V$, true by construction. Thus $S$ is also finitely presented as an $R$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 05B4, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-module, affine reduction; Morphisms Tag 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize

proof.text: By hypothesis $f_*\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation. Clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] makes it quasi-coherent, so clause (b) on $V$ shows that $(f_*\mathcal F)(V)$ is finitely presented over $R$. By the direct-image definition in the statement this is exactly $M=\mathcal F(U)$, and its $R$-action is restriction of its $S$-action through $f^\sharp(V):R\to S$. Consequently $M$ is finitely presented as an $R$-module.

The ring map $R\to S$ satisfies both hypotheses of [lem-trf-finite-extension-module-finite-presentation] by Step 1. Apply its implication from finite presentation over $R$ to finite presentation over $S$ to the $S$-module $M$ of Step 2. This gives that $\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely presented over $\mathcal O_X(U)$.

source.place: Tag 0564, lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension, implication from the base ring to the extension ring

proof.text: Apply clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] to the given quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ and the affine open $U$. The finite presentation of $M$ over $S$ from Step 3 implies that $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation. The opens $f^{-1}V$, for affine opens $V$ of $Y$, cover $X$: for each $x\in X$, choose an affine neighbourhood of $f(x)$ in the scheme $Y$. At each $x$ the local finite presentation on this $U$ supplies exactly the finite free presentation required by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2). Hence $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation on $X$.
